new_exact_application_text.observation: With cable disconnected from ball stud, TestC separately checks cable core return and compression/recovery of spring at throttle-body end of cable. This establishes a cable-end spring function, not the count of shaft-mounted return springs.

specimen.observed: Large coil bank at cable-side lever with bent external wire/leg. A smaller upper coil-looking region and nearby stop screw exist, but hidden endpoints do not allow unambiguous separate spring count or axis assignment.
specimen.limit: No exploded/orthogonal view identifying every independent wire and both anchors.

conclusions.upper_vs_lower_coil_regions: Do not identify both regions as independent coaxial return springs. Perspective, screw-associated coils and other linkage hardware cannot be excluded.
conclusions.cable_end_compression_spring: Separately supported by applicable TestC; not interchangeable with shaft torsion spring.
conclusions.spring_axis_proposal: Y axis through current shaft X394,Z490; model-derived mapping of cable-side coil topology.

proposed_anchor_study.class: explicit geometric estimate; not production anchor locations

stationary.change_needed: New dedicated small tang slot/hole through bracket web; shape/radius to be selected only in later candidate contract. Avoid shield pin atX389,Z514 and shield ear startingZ508.

moving.change_needed: Dedicated tang capture through lever plate, away from ball stud at radial24 mm. Probe is material existence only, not clearance/strength acceptance.

proposed_anchor_study.coil_envelope_trial: Around shaft axis, outboard of hub/pin and inboard of bracket web. Y94–101 and radial7.5–10 mm are exploratory envelopes only, not dimensions or a checked spring; guide/support and every tang route must be solved before CAD acceptance.

dynamics_plan: Hold fixed tang seat in throttle-assembly frame; moving seat follows rigid throttle-moving transform.
Represent torsional deformation; never rotate entire coil rigidly because that detaches stationary anchor.
Keep number of physical wires/count unknown until measured or explicitly scope a one-spring educational abstraction approved by integration owner.

Preserve wire continuity and approximately constant wire length through0–90; winding handedness must oppose opening and retain closing bias. Preload, rate and fatigue cannot be claimed without evidence.
Check 2-degree samples plus endpoint/worst-gap refinement against lever, pin, keyed shaft, housing, bracket, hood, pushpin and cable envelope; verify minimum coil spacing and spring self-clearance.
Negative controls: stationary tang incorrectly parented to moving group; moving tang detached; reversed winding/torque sign; deliberate coil/hub intersection.
Spring return requires physical torque/friction characterization before any safety or functional return claim; source warning requires free return from WOT, not just a visually moving spring.
next_evidence: Applicable manual specimen with both shaft ends and spring bank in several orthogonal views.
Trace each wire from one free end to the other; distinguish coil behind set screw and cable-end compression spring from shaft torsion elements.
Record every stationary notch/post and moving tang tab, unloaded/preloaded angle, coil diameters/wire gauge and count.
